title: introduce sidecar credential shield and safe async-generator ergonomics
author: Oliver Tan
description:
Motivation: Customers report edge cases where long-running streaming consumers lose authentication mid-stream and SDK retry semantics either drop or produce duplicate events. This PR introduces a lightweight sidecar credential shield (opt-in) + safer async-generator surface across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs to make streaming auth lifecycle deterministic and ergonomic. Summary: 1) sidecar credential shield: a thin local agent (in-process shim for OSS SDKs) that serializes credential exchanges, issues short-lived lease tokens, and exposes a small polling/notify API used by SDK connection pools. The shield is intentionally transport-agnostic so it can be adopted by hosted and private deployments. 2) safe async-generator surface: SDKs now expose a cancel-safe async generator / async iterator primitive that guarantees: a) single consumer semantics, b) deterministic backpressure on close(), c) idempotent resume semantics when the shield rotates tokens. 3) ergonomic wrappers: new convenience helpers for common patterns (auto-refresh context manager in Python, StreamHandle in TS, IteratorWithLease in Go) to reduce user code complexity. 4) version bumps: py SDK -> 2.1.0, ts SDK -> 1.28.3, go SDK -> v1.8.0. Checklist: - [x] design doc: ENG-2041 (attached) - [x] implement sidecar shim in SDK core (py/ts/go) - [x] tests: unit + e2e streaming harness - [x] docs: examples and migration guide - [x] release notes - [x] QA: internal smoke tests on Dedicated and Private How it works (brief): the shield maintains a lease table keyed by session id; it serializes rotation so only one inflight rotate request runs per session and broadcasts a short-lived token to connection pool members. SDK stream consumers subscribe to shield events and honor the new token without dropping in-flight message ordering. Sample ergonomic Python wrapper (illustrative):

    class AutoRefreshStream:
        def __init__(self, client, session_id):
            self.client = client
            self.session_id = session_id
        async def __aenter__(self):
            self.handle = await self.client.open_stream(self.session_id)
            return self.handle
        async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
            await self.handle.close()
commits_summary: 7 commits: initial sidecar scaffold; python: hook shield into Pool; ts: introduce StreamHandle + shield subscriber; go: add IteratorWithLease; tests: add e2e harness; docs: streaming auth guide; bump package versions and changelogs
release_notes: Introduce opt-in Sidecar Credential Shield to stabilize streaming auth rotation; add cancel-safe async-generator primitives and ergonomic wrappers across SDKs. Version bumps: python 2.1.0, typescript 1.28.3, go v1.8.0.
review_comments: Maya Chen: overall this looks good. Two concerns: (1) can we avoid a second event loop scheduling in Python when shield does background rotates? (2) add a debug log for token handshake failures so SRE can map to rotate_failures metric.
Author (Oliver Tan): answered Maya - we use the existing SDK loop via call_soon_threadsafe; added debug logs and a unit test that validates no extra loop created.
Priya Patel: TS ergonomics look tight; request: export typed StreamHandle.close(reason?) so callers can signal why they closed. Also suggest a short migration snippet in README.
Author: added optional reason param to StreamHandle.close(reason?: string) and updated README with a migration example.
Arjun Rao: e2e harness showed a flake on python streaming reconnect; found it was a test race (test did not await client.quiesce()). Patched tests and re-ran CI.
QA (Jared Liu): smoke ran against Dedicated cluster-3, rotate_failures=0 over 24h canary; approving for staged rollout.
